decisions.reason: The distribution options and full-gold comparison reference are already captured by the candidate's message-185 INTRODUCE; the proof-format change adds no further state change.
The candidate's existing message-185 MODIFY already narrows the finish candidates to Brushed Metallic and Satin Reflection; the comparison matrix does not otherwise change the finish requirement.
Requesting comparative material proofs does not alter which design assets are locked or the policy requiring their preservation.
The requested comparison format does not change the requirement to provide a short rationale for each design round.
The source specifies proof contents but does not change the accepted image-delivery formats.
Replacing an earlier spacing-comparison task with a material-treatment comparison does not revise the already selected kerning or its underlying rhythm rules.
The material comparison request leaves the shared-baseline requirement unchanged.
Applying champagne gold to the Hero V's right arm in comparison proofs changes color distribution, not the Hero V's geometry.
The instruction to keep non-highlighted elements black does not alter the E and L construction, scale, or architectural design rules.
Coloring the second V's right arm in one comparison option does not change how the second V is geometrically constructed.
The selective-gold comparison does not modify the second V's height relationships or restrained hierarchy role.
Applying champagne gold to the É accent in one option does not change its required peak alignment with the Hero V.
